data.body_html:
Crossing the finish line of Ironman Marbella 2026 is a monumental achievement — 3.8 km of swimming, 180 km of cycling, and a full marathon (42.2 km) along the Costa del Sol. Your muscles deserve more than a hotel bed. A Marbella yacht charter Ironman 2026 recovery day is the ultimate way to soothe sore legs, float in warm Mediterranean water, and celebrate with your crew. Departing from Puerto Banús, our fleet includes everything from a compact 5-pax speedboat to a 29 m superyacht. Prices start at €749 for 2 hours, with skipper, drinks, and snacks included. No hidden costs, no logistics — just you, the sea, and the view of La Concha.

Why a yacht charter beats a spa for Ironman recovery

After 226 km of endurance, your body needs gentle movement and zero impact. Floating in the sea at 21°C (October average) reduces inflammation and eases muscle stiffness. A yacht charter gives you controlled exposure to sunlight (vitamin D for bone repair), fresh sea air, and the option to nap on a padded sunbed. Unlike a crowded spa, you control the environment: music volume, shade levels, and stop locations. Our skippers know the calmest coves — Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés — where the water is glassy and quiet. And you can toast your finish with a glass of cava, guilt-free.

Our recovery-day fleet: from intimate to superyacht

We operate 17 boats from Puerto Banús, each with a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and a full drinks-and-snacks package. For a small group of athletes (up to 5 pax), the Dubhe (8 m) or Mariah SX21 (6.4 m) are nimble and affordable. For 10–12 pax, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6 m) or Mangusta 80 (24 m) offer flybridge lounges and spacious aft decks — ideal for stretching out. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B boats (Mangusta 80 variants) are €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and include a jet ski for anyone feeling energetic. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

Best recovery itineraries from Puerto Banús

Your skipper will tailor the route to your energy level, but here are three proven options:

  • 2-hour mini cruise — Head west to Cala del Faro (3 NM). Drop anchor for a 15-minute float, then cruise back past the Golden Mile. Perfect for a quick post-race unwind.
  • 4-hour half-day — Sail to Cala Cortés (5 NM) for a longer swim stop, then motor east to Cabopino for lunch at a beach chiringuito. Includes light snacks on board.
  • 8-hour full day — Push to Estepona (12 NM) with a stop at the Río Verde estuary. Lunch at a waterfront restaurant, afternoon nap on deck, sunset return to Puerto Banús.

All itineraries include unlimited soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava. If you want a specific meal (e.g., grilled fish or paella), let us know 24 hours ahead — we can arrange catering.

What to bring and what to leave behind

Bring swimwear, a towel, sunscreen (reef-safe preferred), sunglasses, and a light jacket for the evening breeze. Leave behind: stress, training schedules, and nutrition timetables. The boat provides all drinks and snacks, plus safety equipment. If you have dietary restrictions (e.g., gluten-free or vegan), mention it when booking — we stock alternatives. No need to bring cash; everything is included in the charter price.

How to book your Ironman recovery day charter

Booking is simple: send us a WhatsApp message with your preferred date, boat type, group size, and any special requests. We’ll confirm availability and send a secure payment link. For Ironman weekend, we recommend booking at least two weeks in advance — boats fill quickly. All prices include Spanish IVA (21%) and there are no hidden fees. Your charter departs from Puerto Banús, just 10 minutes from the finish line. For more details on our full fleet and pricing, visit our Marbella yacht charter homepage.

Combine your charter with other recovery activities

Many athletes pair a morning yacht charter with an afternoon massage at a Golden Mile spa, or a gentle yoga session on the beach at Cabopino. The marina at Puerto Banús has several restaurants serving post-race nutrition (think grilled fish, fresh salads, and smoothie bowls). If you’re staying in Marbella for a few days, consider a sunset charter on the second day — the light on La Concha is spectacular. For more ideas, read our guide to Ironman recovery day packages.
